column31: I book with Loyalty when looking for hotels, flights, and cruises above all. I took a 24 night vacation that included 4 legs. I started with 2 nights at a Marriott in Vancouver before boarding the Ovation of the Seas’ 11 night Alaskan Sailing. Unique experiences such as one off itineraries and special occasions make for far more enjoyable and memorable trips than the standard rotating sailings. After that it ended in Seattle where we spent 2 nights before flying to Hawaii for 8 nights at Aulani A Disney Resort and Spa using my Disney Vacation Club points. We split our time between the resort and exploring the island. The number of unique experiences that aren’t repeated adds so much to the memory and experience. Having multiple legs to offer different experiences and types of vacations within a single trip ensures it stays fun and exciting. Getting quality and value out of as little spending though is the key to enabling an incredible trip like this. Something I’ve done several times now in different ways.

column31: We love to eat and drink our way through a city, no matter how long we visit. Our last trip was a long weekend trip to Chicago. We dined at Girl and the Goat; had drinks (and dinner) at the Chef's Table at the Aviary. We saw the Rolling Stones in concert, and finished the evening with a late night dinner (11:30pm) at Avec. We had a late brunch at Stephanie Izard's newest restaurant Cabra, on the roof of the Hoxton, and strolled down to the Lazy Bird speakeasy in the basement. We recently had a similar visit to Kansas City, but it was even more indicative of how we spend our time in a city... On the first night in any city, we belly up to the best bar (or restaurant) in the city, chat up the bartender, ask their opinion about the restaurants we were thinking of visiting, get recommendations for the rest of our time there. Our best meal was at Corvino Supper Club, where we sat at the bar for dinner. The bartenders made amazing cocktails, and they helped us pick the best dishes. And they didn't want us to leave without trying seaweed donuts, so they sent us out a dish. They even slipped us a nice thank you note before we left. For us, it's all about the experience and the great people we meet. It doesn't matter if the trip is one of our Thursday - Sunday "weekend" getaways, or a week-long vacation. We love talking to the local people and experiencing their world through food and drink.

column31: We love cruising in warm climates but have already been to most of the traditional ports in the Caribbean and have been on most of the ship types of interest that sail from Florida. So we booked our first suite on Celebrity on an average ship on an average itinerary, which made it an affordable trial run. What we found that it wasn’t the extra space that was enticing, although it was nice. But rather it was the amenities and attentive service that made the experience our favorite cruise ever. Michaels Club access, reserved seats at the theatre, a pillow menu, upgraded room service menu, a fabulous attendant/butler who kept our minibar stocked with only our favorite beverages, a bathtub with window, amazing products, a couple suite-exclusive restaurants, open bar, internet, tips included, even $300 cash that we used toward swimming with dolphins and a visit to the water park at Atlantis. After that cruise experience with Celebrity,  I am having a hard time considering anything less. We LOVED that the casino was nonsmoking, there were only a few children, and the louder party people seemed less in my face, because I think in part, the suite class experiences created a new cruise experience entirely. Looking at other cruise lines and it seems a suite is mostly just extra space but Celebrity really gives you a lot of value and I dare say we probably would have spent the same amount on a standard balcony cabin had we had to pay for all the extras separately in the end. Instead, we walked off the ship at the end of our vacation with virtually no significant ship-board charges. Now that’s a great feeling!

column31: Sadly, our last trip overseas was over a year ago but we enjoyed a quick trip to New York City for a bit of excitement last month. My travel companion, Steve and I tend to rotate our holidays around food and beverage- we love exploring cities/cultures via their local cuisine. We tend to find a great locals only watering hole, noteworthy "like mamma makes" nibbles, and at least one special occasion/fine dining spot. We love luxury (service is very important to us on all levels with every place we encounter- its a lost art!) but tend to lean towards funky spaces, more intimate/boutique places with quirky perks and a convenient location. Our trip to New York entailed hitting some old school city food spots as well as some of the current hot spots. We love exploring the New York Public Library (we are also big on design, architecture, art and history), a stroll through Central Park, and a Broadway show is a must whenever we are in the city- music is a huge part of our lives so we tend to see a good 'ole musical! This trip we went to "The Prom"- so fun! And, speaking of music... can't go to New York without a visit to Bemelmans Bar at The Carlyle Hotel- Art Deco details, Ludwig Bemelmans whimsical murals, timeless entertainment all while clasping a perfectly crafted Manhattan complete with a sidecar- heaven. This particular getaway was to celebrate a birthday but we are no strangers to adventure (I have bungee jumped out of a hot air balloon, skydived, etc; Steve is a scuba diver, avid outdoors man). We enjoy just about anything and look forward to taking our adventures to the next level on our Virgin Voyage next year!

column31: My recent vacation was on a Royal Caribbean Cruise. My husband and I were on the Oasis of the Seas and traveled a “Western Caribbean” route which stopped at RC’s private destination Labadee, Haiti, Falmouth, Jamaica, and Cozumel, Mexico. We had a blast and the ship was the best part of the vacation. We had our best time in Jamaica forging our own path and exploring the local town. We ate in an authentic restaurant and had Jerk Chicken that was absolutely delicious! Our stop in Labadee was disappointing and we just went back to the ship. Our stop in Cozumel was fun and interesting, however, we made the mistake of eating at a restaurant that was promoted by the cruise ship and was greatly disappointed. The food and experience was solely crafted for the tourist and thus lacking in authenticity. We learned our lesson to never done at a restaurant recommended by the cruise line. Our experience aboard the ship was amazing. Everything about the ship was amazing. From the food, the entertainment, and overall experience/service was fantastic. We especially loved the experience at the uncharge restaurants, but given that we payed more for that experience it was expected.The aspects of the trip we were most were most disappointed about were: A) The mattress was REALLY firm and even after our attendant added padding, it was only just bearable but overall still uncomfortable.B) Almost every five minutes, it seemed the Cruise Line was throwing some sort of “sale” or promoting shopping on board. Also, the “educational seminars” are really sales pitches paid for by the shopping locations at each destination. Granted, I did actually manage to glean some usable information from them.C) There is an up-charge for EVERYTHING! We already paid a lot for the vacation and we really felt like the cruise line was trying to fleece us for every last penny. Upon reflection, just when we thought we scored a great deal for the trip, we actually ended up paying a lot more.

column31: My most recent vacation was a Azmara cruise, from Tokyo, Japan to Anchorage, Alaska.I spent a few days in Tokyo beforehand, spending a day with a friend driving around the countryside and staying in an Onsen, after staying in the Tokyo Palace Station hotel.  My wife joined me after that, we spent a few days at Disney staying at the MIracosta hotel, with a lot of Disney time but taking some day trips into Tokyo including the Digital Art Museum, very spectacular!We made our way to the cruise port by bus, and set sail northward.Along the cruise, we made two stops at a northern Japanese island, where each location we had arranged a private tour with several other people joining in.  Although we saw some common sights across the island, one of our favorite stops turned out to be a small farm the tour guide knew about with a soft serve store, one of the best soft serve ice cream cones I've ever had - with a beautiful view outside of a distant snowy volcano across a lush grassy hillside.Leaving Japan behind, we sailed on to the Kamchatka peninsula in Russia, where we had a private off-road tour arranged with a professional off-raid racer and local guide... we drove through the still snowy hills around the volcanic area of the town and enjoyed some nice overviews of the sea from on-high, including a picnic in the wilderness.After the stop in Russia, we kept heading north and east, to cross the Bering Sea to reach the Aleutian Islands.  Happily the whole time from Japan to the Aleutians we had amazingly good weather, with extremely calm seas so that even on this northern cruise we could enjoy some time out on the balcony of our room, admiring fantastic sunsets with volcanoes on distant land, and birds skimming the smooth seas besides our ship.Eventually reaching the Aleutians, we sailed along the island chain heading toward the Alaskan mainland - there is more to the journey (including some amazing kayaking) but this box is out of space.  :-)

column31: My last vacation was a 7-day cruise on MSC Seaside in May 2019. It was a wonderful trip. It was my seventh cruise overall. I've sailed 5 times on NCL, 1 time on Royal Caribbean, and this was my first time on MSC. I enjoyed the vibe onboard. While my heart is still with NCL, the international feel of the crew and passengers on MSC provided a great experience. All of my cruises so far have been solo. NCL does a great job with solo travelers in providing opportunities to meet others with the studio cabins, studio lounge, and solo hosts. Royal Caribbean did not provide any type of positive solo experience. MSC's was mediocre.While I do really enjoy certain destinations (such as Bermuda), my primary focus on my cruises is the ship itself. I love the physical spaces and the thrill of escaping to another world onboard. I especially love sea days and am excited to see what Scarlet Lady offers onboard to facilitate that escape. What happens on the ship stays on the ship, so I challenge you to woo me, Virgin. ;-)

column34: You offer solo cabins and seem to really want us onboard! Other lines actively discourage solo travelers (especially in charging double prices for solo cabins).
column36: You're differentiating yourselves. I do love some aspects of existing cruise lines like the parties, innovative designs, and social opportunities. But many of them still retain the stodgy old traditional junk to keep old cruisers happy. I don't pack formal clothes for my vacation, and I'm certainly not going to hand my money over to a line that wants to shame me into tuxxing up for dinner on a formal night. Bring out the drag queens. Let me express the absolute best version of myself. Let us escape and be whatever we want to be, without judgment! The Virgin brand embraces that outlook, and I'm hopeful that fellow cruisers feel the same way. I also like how your advertising is unapologetically bold. On the cruising forums that I frequent, it's clear that traditional cruisers who like modesty and subtlety are getting the message that this line isn't for them. They can go elsewhere. This ship is for people like me.

column31: Our last trip was to take in NYC during the Christmas season.  We attended the Christmas Spectacular at Radio City Music Hall (and were blown away-how magical!).  We also did a private SUV tour of the city, that stopped at several places that the locals value.  Our driver was amazing. He was a life-long New Yorker who narrated as he drove.  We went to Christmas markets and saw so much in four hours.  Stopped for local foods and just loved it.  We took my mom, who had never been to NYC, and she was in awe of it all.  We stayed at the Marriott Marquis on Times Square and also attended Wicked on Broadway.  We took the architectural and art tour of Rockefeller Center.  And we ate, and ate, and ate our way through the City.  Junior's Cheesecake every damn day baby!  Along with so many others in Little Italy, Hell's Kitchen, etc etc.  When I am on vacation, I like to indulge and experience as much as possible.  We also went to the Museum of Modern Art to take in some of our faves.  Yes, people from Iowa have culture.  That is just a sampling of what we did while in NYC.  As I think about this, NYC wasn't our last trip.  I guess we went to the Dominican Republic in March.  But that was with a group of our friends, and our only purpose on that trip was to sit on the beach, laugh and drink.  Priceless memories, but not much that I should divulge there.  We did rent a party boat for our group one day.  I may have had another boat chanting my name when we met them at the common stop where all the boats park and party.

column31: I went with a friend on a 7 day Eastern Mediterranean cruise on MSC Sinfonia, and spent 3 nights in Venice prior to departing on the cruise. I really appreciated being on an Italian line, to get a true European flavor. We made sure to make the most of exploring each port (Split, Santorini, Mykonos, Dubrovnik, and Ancona), usually with an organized excursion. Our shipboard experience was wonderful as well. We chose a mid priced cabin and experience, which worked well for us. We got good value for what we spent.I would take this trip (or similar) again in a heartbeat!

column31: My last vacation was a cruise on a giant ship, and it kinda sucked (so many kids, so much nickel-and-diming, never again), so I'll choose to share the one before that. My husband and I went backpacking around the UK for two weeks. "Backpacking" in that we carried all our stuff in one backpack each, making it really easy to hop on trains and get from place to place. But we stayed in high-end hotels in London, Edinburgh, and Glasgow, and we stayed in the nicest room at the nicest B&B in Cornwall. We each had a couple of easy-care dress-up outfits, too, so we could go to high-end restaurants in out-of-the-way special places, afternoon tea at Fortnum & Mason, and theatre in the West End -- hotel rooms have irons! We stopped in Glasgow at the halfway point of our trip to do all our laundry -- the laundrette wasn't near the hotel, and we didn't stay anywhere that had overnight laundry service (we weren't anywhere long enough to send out our wash), so we got on the hop-on-hop-off tour bus *with our full laundry bags*, and halfway through the tour, hopped off, tossed our laundry into a machine at the laundrette, went to get lunch, went back to pick up our clothes (the nice lady running the place swapped them to the dryer for us), and then we got back on the tour bus at the stop where we'd gotten off, and finished the tour. Then, near the end of our trip, we took a three-day cruise out of Southampton that took us to Brussels and Rotterdam, where we booked food tours with local guides. Mmmmmm. That was a great trip. We met some cool like-minded people on those food tours, too.

column31: We live in Palm Beach in the winter and on Lake Harvey, Vermont, in the summer. So our vacations are not to escape our "places" but to escape our routines and busy day to day activities.We do take a break during our transitions - we like to stop and spend time in Cornelius NC on Lake Norman, and rent a nice home or condo on the lake there when we do so. Not really a vacation, but a time out between two very different lives.Vacations fall more along the lines of a stay at the Four Seasons commingled with a stay at a rural indigenous hotel in Costa Rica, or at the Scarlet Huntington in San Francisco, the XV Beacon in Boston, Chateau Frontenac in Quebec City, the Montage anywhere before it became too expensive, and the like. We have enjoyed cruises throughout the Caribbean on the smaller cruise lines, and are looking forward our inaugural cruise with you. Cuba would have been nice, that's why we chose the 2nd voyage instead of your first, but I'm sure we will still enjoy our experience. I lived in Europe for some time when I was. young, but have not returned since. So that is definitely on our agenda over the coming years. Revisiting where I lived, going those places I haven't been, spending enough time to settle in. And although I certainly prefer the luxury of the higher end hotels, other alternatives such as home exchange or the like, may afford us more time, and a bit more immersion in the local culture. We'll see. Perhaps a river cruise as well. Many friends have spoken highly of their vacations down the Danube, and the rivers of Thailand and Vietnam.The main impediment to all of the above is the lack of ease of air travel to embark on the vacation. That is of course one of the reasons your cruise appeals, we just get in the car and drive down to Miami and board the ship and go. Perfect!Karla Corneliuskarlacornelius@comcast.net
